title: The Horizon of New Lagos
premise: Wren Oyelaran, a xenolinguist whose dreams have abandoned human speech, pilots the long route between worlds that no longer speak to one another. When a distress signal arrives in a language extinct for two centuries, he discovers it is a forgery—his own creation, resurrected by his estranged sister to keep two hostile fleets from open war over the colony world of New Lagos. To keep the lie alive, Wren must translate, embellish, and sustain a dead tongue faster than the fleets' cryptographers can expose it, all while the truth of what really happened on New Lagos threatens the found family of smugglers and refugees who trust him. In the end, Wren chooses truth over loyalty: he broadcasts the genuine last recordings of the extinct civilization, forcing both fleets to reckon with a shared guilt—and giving the survivors of New Lagos a voice of their own.
about_author: Yara Sandoval is a former shipping-lane cartographer who spent a decade charting routes through contested orbital corridors before turning to fiction. She writes from a houseboat off the Atlantic coast, where she claims the tide speaks a language older than any fleet.

chapters.title: The Long Silence
chapters.summary: Wren Oyelaran, running cargo and translation work on the fringes, dreams in no human tongue and wakes lonely among the crew of the freighter Kindly Hours—his found family of misfits. A distress signal arrives in Ashanti-Meridian, a language dead two hundred years, and only Wren can read it. POV: Wren. Beat: restless isolation cracking into wonder and dread.

chapters.title: A Voice from the Drowned Archive
chapters.summary: Wren deciphers the signal: a colony on New Lagos claiming attack, begging both the Concord fleet and the Meridian flotilla to stand down. He realizes the grammar is flawless—too flawless. Someone alive still speaks Ashanti-Meridian. POV: Wren. Beat: intellectual thrill curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Sister Who Speaks the Dead
chapters.summary: Following the signal's origin, Wren finds Adaeze, his estranged sister, broadcasting from a derelict archive ship. She forged the distress call to stall two fleets massing over New Lagos, where their parents died in the first skirmish. She begs him to help her keep the lie alive. POV: Wren. Beat: reunion laced with old wounds and reluctant awe.

chapters.title: Kindly Hours, Unkind Choices
chapters.summary: Wren returns to his crew and conceals the forgery, asking them to run supplies to New Lagos under neutral flags. Navigator Sefu grows suspicious; medic Ilse quietly covers for him. The Kindly Hours becomes complicit without knowing why. POV: Sefu. Beat: loyalty tested by half-truths; warmth shadowed by deceit.

chapters.title: Cryptographers at the Gate
chapters.summary: A Concord interrogation vessel boards the Kindly Hours. Wren bluffs his way through a live translation session, improvising in Ashanti-Meridian so convincingly that the examiner flags him as a native speaker—an asset to be conscripted. POV: Wren. Beat: terror sharpened into performance; a lie deepening its roots.

chapters.title: What the Colony Actually Said
chapters.summary: On New Lagos, Wren finds the real recordings: the extinct civilization's final transmissions, sealed by both fleets because they reveal the colony's destruction was a joint accident both sides covered up. Adaeze's lie accidentally protects the truth's perpetrators. POV: Adaeze. Beat: moral vertigo—her justice is feeding the guilty.

chapters.title: The Grammar of War
chapters.summary: Both fleets converge on New Lagos, each believing the other fired first. Adaeze's forged signal frays under cryptographic scrutiny; she works herself to collapse sustaining it. Wren must choose: extend the lie and buy evacuation time, or detonate it and risk immediate war. POV: Wren. Beat: desperation, love for his sister at war with his crew's safety.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax. Wren seizes the archive ship's array and transmits the authentic last recordings of the extinct civilization to both fleets at once—their shared crime, in their shared dead language. Fleets freeze mid-attack. Adaeze, betrayed and freed, helps him translate the final passage live as commanders listen. POV: Adaeze. Beat: devastating, cathartic exposure; truth as the only ceasefire.

chapters.title: The Fleet That Stopped
chapters.summary: In the stunned aftermath, both fleets withdraw to joint inquiry; the crews of New Lagos finally speak for themselves. Wren faces charges but the Kindly Hours' crew testifies for him, and Ilse's quiet records of the evacuation tip the tribunal toward mercy. POV: Ilse. Beat: exhausted relief; found family holding the line for one of its own.

chapters.title: Dreaming in New Lagos
chapters.summary: Months later, Wren teaches Ashanti-Meridian to the colony's children—no longer a dead language but an inherited one. He dreams again, and this time the dream has words. Adaeze, pardoned, runs messages between the fleets; the Kindly Hours takes on a new route. POV: Wren. Beat: quiet, earned peace; a voice restored, a family whole.
